name: Musawwarat Great Hafir
summary: The Great Hafir at Musawwarat es-Sufra, a large dug and embanked reservoir built in the sixth to fourth centuries BCE to catch seasonal desert runoff.
description: Large embanked reservoir with an excavated basin, capturing Wadi es-Sufra runoff for local water storage.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.
why: The site lies in dry savanna away from the Nile, so seasonal wadi runoff had to be captured and stored for use through the dry season.

date.label: Sixth–fourth centuries BCE
date.basis: Project chronology explicitly reports the radiocarbon-constrained construction interval.

events.statement: The Musawwarat project dates construction of the Great Hafir between the sixth and fourth centuries BCE.
events.population: The Kushite Musawwarat religious-site water users and maintainers
events.caveats: Century bounds express the reported interval, not exact construction endpoints. This does not date every inlet, duct or subsequent use.

evidence.supports: Radiocarbon-based construction interval, distinct from later Meroitic occupation.

date.label: by c. 350 CE (Meroitic use inferred)
date.basis: The project describes the reservoir feeding the Great Enclosure within its Meroitic occupation context; the endpoint is an approximate contextual horizon.

events.statement: The Great Hafir stored local water used in the Musawwarat religious-site system.
events.population: The Kushite Musawwarat religious-site water users and maintainers
events.caveats: The Great Hafir’s construction is radiocarbon-constrained to the 6th–4th centuries BCE; neither its original commissioning nor the ducts’ precise age is individually dated. The 350 CE endpoint is only a broad Meroitic contextual estimate, not a hard archaeological cutoff.

evidence.supports: The project describes the reservoir, 85 m inlet and water ducts supplying the Great Enclosure in its Meroitic context.
